mcqs.learning_point: Explaining why a material belongs to a group
mcqs.question: Which statement best explains why a wooden spoon is placed in the group of non‑metallic objects rather than metallic objects?

options.A: Wood conducts electricity better than metals.
options.B: Wood is made of organic fibers and does not conduct electricity, unlike metals.
options.C: Wood is heavier than most metals.
options.D: Wood has a shiny surface like many metals.

mcqs.answer: Wood is made of organic fibers and does not conduct electricity, unlike metals.
mcqs.explanation: Wood is a non‑metallic material; it is composed of organic fibers, is an insulator, and does not conduct electricity. These properties distinguish it from metallic objects, which are typically conductive and have metallic bonds. Option B correctly states these reasons, while the other options describe properties that are either false or irrelevant for classification.

mcqs.learning_point: Using classification to identify suitable materials
mcqs.question: A scientist needs a material for a water‑carrying pipe that will not rust or react with water. Which classification property should be used to select the most suitable material?
mcqs.explanation: For a water pipe, the most important property is resistance to corrosion, because the material will be in constant contact with water. Plastic or certain stainless steels have high corrosion resistance. Magnetic property, electrical conductivity, and hardness are not directly related to the pipe’s durability in water. Hence option C is correct.

mcqs.question: Which property is most appropriate when classifying objects as magnetic or non‑magnetic?
mcqs.explanation: Magnetism directly indicates whether an object is attracted to a magnet, making it the suitable property for this classification. Color, hardness, and taste have no relevance to magnetic behavior.

mcqs.question: If we group the items glass, wood, plastic sheet, and metal spoon based only on transparency, which items will be placed together?
mcqs.explanation: Transparency is the single property used. Glass and a clear plastic sheet are transparent, while wood and a metal spoon are opaque. Therefore they belong to the same group, making option A correct. The other options either mix transparent with opaque items or ignore the property.

mcqs.learning_point: Creating groups using more than one property
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes grouping objects using more than one property?

options.A: Objects are placed together if they share at least one of the selected properties.
options.B: Objects are placed together only if they share all the selected properties.
options.C: Objects are grouped randomly after a single property is chosen.
options.D: Objects are grouped based on their size only, regardless of other properties.

mcqs.answer: Objects are placed together only if they share all the selected properties.
mcqs.explanation: When multiple properties are used for classification, an object must satisfy every chosen property to belong to a particular group. Option B captures this definition. Option A describes single‑property grouping, while C and D are unrelated to multi‑property classification.

mcqs.learning_point: Explaining why a material belongs to a group
mcqs.question: A rubber ball is placed in the group of 'flexible materials'. Which reason best explains this classification?

options.B: Rubber can be stretched and returns to its original shape.

mcqs.answer: Rubber can be stretched and returns to its original shape.
mcqs.explanation: Flexibility refers to the ability of a material to deform under force and recover its shape. Rubber exhibits this behavior, making option B correct. Conductivity, weight, and transparency are unrelated to flexibility.

mcqs.learning_point: Using classification to identify suitable materials
mcqs.question: Which material would be most suitable for the handle of a kitchen knife if we classify materials based on hardness (low) and heat resistance (high)?
mcqs.explanation: A good knife handle should not be too hard (to avoid cracking) and must resist heat from cooking. Soft wood has low hardness and reasonable heat resistance, fitting both criteria. Hard steel and ceramic are too hard, while glass is brittle and not heat‑resistant enough for a handle.

mcqs.question: A teacher wants to sort classroom waste into recyclable and non‑recyclable piles. Which property should be selected for the classification?
mcqs.explanation: Recyclability depends primarily on the material composition; paper, plastic, and metal are recyclable, while many other materials are not. Color, size, or weight do not determine whether an item can be recycled, making option B the correct choice.
